title: Probabilistic SLO negotiation and regional rebalance playbook
creator: Marco Li
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, model-and-route-aware SLO/SLI declaration format and an error-budget reconciliation algorithm that supports probabilistic negotiation between regions and model variants. This playbook documents SLI choices (latency quantiles, request-quality signals, and functional correctness where applicable), how to compute composed error budgets across model variants and regions, and deterministic fallback/rebalance heuristics driven by probabilistic signals rather than rigid thresholds. Motivation: current per-endpoint SLOs are brittle during cross-region incidents and during incremental rollouts of quantized variants. Teams need a way to (1) express joint quality/latency SLOs for routes backed by multiple model variants, (2) reconcile error-budget consumption dynamically across regions, and (3) pick graceful load-shedding / circuit-breaker actions that preserve highest-priority contracts.
decision_summary: Use a dual-axis SLI: P95 latency (ms) + request-level quality score (0-1) derived from promptset evals and runtime checks.
Define per-route composite SLO as a weighted target: e.g., 95% of requests must meet latency <= X OR quality >= Y; weights configurable by route.

Implement probabilistic error-budget rebalancer: regions expose burn-rate distributions, central controller computes probability of cross-region rescue and issues graceful degradation orders when rescue probability < 10%.
Favor variant demotion (reduce traffic to a variant) over full route throttling; demotion uses soft limits and retractable credit accounting.
Circuit breakers operate in two modes: fast-fail (hard threshold for infra failures) and graceful-degrade (quality-driven, uses sampled signals and Bayesian smoothing).
Keep SLO declarations machine-readable (YAML/JSON) and attach metadata: route_priority, expected_input_size_dist, quality_probe_set_id, fallback_variant_order.
Expose human-facing coffeebreak dashboards and runbooks for oncall to understand probabilistic signals and override policies.
Security review not required for control-plane logic, but audit logging is mandatory for any automated traffic rebalancing action.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLO/SLI schema published in Confluence and validated by two product teams.
Automated tests that simulate regional burn-rate scenarios and demonstrate probabilistic rebalance decisions in staging.
A Grafana dashboard and alerting policy that surfaces burn-rate distribution and rebalance recommendations.
A small canary rollout of the rebalancer against non-critical routes with rollback hooks implemented in the console.
work_items: Spec: machine-readable SLO schema and sample route manifests (ENG + PM review)
Implementation: burn-rate sampler + Bayesian smoothing service (runtime infra)
CLI/API: endpoints to submit per-region burn snapshots and request quality probes
Console: dashboard panels and suggested action buttons (Canary toggle + force override)
Chaos testing: multi-region latency/failure injection experiments
Docs: runbook, how-to guide for PMs on configuring weights and probe sets
